content.text:
I found only one night of Google sleep data for last week, so I can't give you a real weekly summary.

**Date range used:** Monday Oct 26 through Sunday Nov 1, 2026 (New York time). I used Nov 2 as today, per the system date. The environment also listed Oct 30, which would put "last week" at Oct 19–25. If that's your real date, tell me and I'll rerun it.

**What's stored locally for that range:**
- **Sunday Nov 1:** one sleep session, 420 minutes (7 hours) asleep. It started Oct 31 at 11:00 PM and ended Nov 1 at 7:00 AM, local time.
- **Monday through Saturday:** no sleep records. Missing days are not the same as zero sleep. They just aren't in the local database.

**Overnight reporting dates:** Google labels each sleep session with the calendar date you woke up, not the date you went to bed. So the 11 PM Oct 31 to 7 AM Nov 1 session counts as Nov 1. A Monday-to-Sunday filter therefore includes a Sunday-night sleep only if you woke up on Sunday, and a Monday night is counted under Monday's wake-up date.

**Why the data is so thin:**
- Google isn't connected on this machine. The connection check reports no verified API connection and no stored tokens, so I can't pull more sleep data.
- The local database only holds one sleep record in total, and it was loaded by a synthetic parser. Its timestamps are from a test source, so don't treat it as a real measurement.
- Only 3 days of Google step data exist locally (Oct 1–3), so there's nothing else to compare against.

**To get a real summary:** run `ghealth auth login` to reconnect Google, then I can import sleep history and redo the weekly summary. While the Google consent screen is in Testing mode, tokens expire after 7 days, so you may need to log in again each week.
